title: Literary Language Mashup: Curating Fictions with Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.21649v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: In this paper, we propose an alternative approach to human evaluation of literary fictions by employing LLMs themselves as evaluators within the GrAImes framework. We apply this methodology to assess human-written and AI-generated microfictions in Spanish, to five PhD professors in literature and sixteen literary enthusiasts, and to short stories in both Spanish and English. By comparing the evaluations performed by LLMs with those of human judges, we examine the degree of alignment and divergence between both perspectives, thereby assessing the feasibility of LLMs as auxiliary literary evaluators. Our analysis focuses on the alignment of responses from LLMs with those of human evaluators, providing insights into the potential of LLMs in literary assessment. translated_title: 文学语言混搭：利用大语言模型策划小说
translated_abstract: 本文提出了一种替代性的文学虚构作品人工评估方法，即在GrAImes框架内采用大语言模型（LLMs）本身作为评估者。我们将这一方法应用于评估西班牙语的人工写作与AI生成的微型小说，评估对象包括五位文学博士教授和十六位文学爱好者，同时也评估了西班牙语和英语的短篇小说。通过比较LLM所进行的评估与人类评委的评估，我们考察了两种视角之间的契合度与分歧程度，从而评估LLM作为辅助文学评估者的可行性。我们的分析重点关注LLM的回答与人类评估者回答的一致性，为LLM在文学评估中的潜力提供了洞见。所开展的实验表明，尽管LLM不能被视为文学微型小说和短篇小说评估中人类评委的替代品（Krippendorff一致性系数显示……
tldr: 本文提出在GrAImes框架中让大语言模型充当文学评估者，通过对比LLM与人类评委（文学教授及爱好者）对西班牙语和英语小说的评估，发现LLM虽可作为辅助文学评估工具，但无法替代人类评委。
en_tdlr: This paper employs LLMs as evaluators within the GrAImes framework to assess Spanish and English fictions, and by comparing LLM evaluations with those of human judges (literature professors and enthusiasts), finds that LLMs can serve as auxiliary literary evaluators but cannot substitute for human judges.
